name: Why do mobile home interior doors stick or fail to latch properly?

mainEntity.name: Why do mobile home interior doors stick or fail to latch properly?

acceptedAnswer.text: Manufactured homes settle over time, which shifts the wall studs and knocks rectangular door frames out of square. Because mobile homes rest on piers or tie-downs, ground moisture and seasonal temperature shifts cause subtle leveling changes that traditional foundation-built homes do not experience as dramatically. As the frame racks, door latches fail to align with strike plates, and the door sticks along the top or bottom edges. In many cases, addressing a sticking door requires adjusting the frame shims and re-securing door casing rather than shaving down the door itself.
acceptedAnswer.description: Mobile homes shift on their supports over time, distorting the thin wall framing and knocking door jambs out of square so latches no longer catch.
